subject: Model recommendations + context-window observations — summary & follow-ups

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Quick recap and next steps from this morning's call

Hi Maya / Evan —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Short recap + proposed next steps so we can move to a short evaluation quickly.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Use case: multi-section clinical note ingestion (lab reports + consults) with structured section-level and global summaries for downstream search and triage.
- Primary concern: summary fidelity when a single patient record exceeds 50k tokens — you saw truncation artifacts in your current pipeline.
- Success criteria you mentioned: (1) per-note summary precision on entity extraction (meds/diagnoses) > 95% relative to your baseline, (2) human-rated summarization fidelity >= 4/5 across a 50-sample set, (3) latency SLO ~ < 1.2s/1k tokens for synchronous summary endpoints.
- Non-functional: data residency + encryption-at-rest requirements, and need for audit logs.

Proposed evaluation plan (short):
1) Redwood will run a 1-week pilot against three model-config variants you can choose from: RIS-compact-32k (quantized), RIS-extended-64k (FP16), and RIS-precision-65b (higher quality, larger memory). We will provide per-token cost estimates and latency baselines.
2) We run two benchmark flows: (A) chunk+stitch with 1k overlap (cheap, good recall), and (B) progressive summarization (iterative condensation) to preserve narrative fidelity (better for long context but higher compute).
3) We'll use the prompt-sets attached (prompt-sets-v1.md) and the small seed dataset you agreed to send.

Attachments: prompt-sets-v1.md (prompt templates + expected outputs), context-window-benchmarks.csv (sample perf numbers from similar pilots).

Open questions / asks from your side:
- Please share 6–8 representative notes (de-identified) and one example of a record that previously truncated badly.
- Confirmation on whether the pilot can run on your VPC or we should use Hosted with an aggressive data retention policy.

Suggested next steps:
- You share sample docs by end of week (EOD Fri).
- We schedule a 30-minute sync next Wed (10/21) to review pilot design and sample mapping.

Optional meeting slots: Wed 10/21 10:00–10:30 PT or 14:00–14:30 PT.

Thanks — I’ll loop Rishi for pricing/contract quick answers and Monica for the evaluation runbook.

—
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Quick recap and next steps from this morning's call

Maya — quick answers to your operational questions and a couple of notes on model choices: 

PHI: pseudonymized tokens are OK for initial model-fit runs, but for any signed pilot that writes logs we recommend fully de-identified samples or using your VPC with customer-managed KMS. We can accept S3 links with encryption and an access window.

KMS: yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for our Private deployment. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer-provided keys (Bring Your Own Key) — I'll share the spec sheet in the drive link below.

Model recommendations (based on fidelity vs cost trade-offs):
- RIS-compact-32k (quantized) — best cost / latency for chunk+stitch; expect occasional entity drop if chunk boundaries split entity spans. Good baseline for throughput testing.
- RIS-extended-64k (FP16) — middle ground: larger window reduces stitching artifacts and keeps more inter-section context; recommended first pass for your 50k+ notes.
- RIS-precision-65b (full) — highest fidelity for narrative summarization and edge-case reasoning; use if we see fail-cases in sampling.

Mitigations for truncation/fidelity:
1) Dynamic windowing with section-aware chunking (we keep headings intact).
2) Progressive summarization pipeline: summarize per-section -> synthesize -> final condensation (keeps narrative coherence).
3) KV-cache prefixing for repeated context (patient metadata) across requests.
4) Confidence-scoring and a fallback policy to RIS-precision-65b when the summary confidence is low.

Benchmarks & monitoring: see attached context-window-benchmarks.csv for per-token latency and avg Rouge-like fidelity scores from a comparable 40k note set. We'll also enable a delta-quality alert in Redwood Console that monitors the evaluation prompt-set outputs against your human labels and fires if quality drops >4%.

Action items (owners):
- Maya: share 6 de-identified notes + one truncated example (deadline: 2026-10-16 EOD).
- Olga: schedule the 10/21 10:00 PT slot and share calendar invite (owner: Olga).
- Monica: prepare the eval runbook and the Drive folder with the prompt variants and the small harness for scoring (owner: Monica).
- Rishi: draft pilot commercial terms (flat pilot fee + overage estimator) and share a short SOW.

Drive / docs: https://redwood-internal.drive/s/1a2b3c/context-window-benchmarks (contains prompt-sets-v1.md and the sample harness).

I'll be available on Friday for any quick contract/pricing clarifications.

—Rishi
